{"id":"persona-vvs2.4","title":"Named pipe listener and stream","description":"The second transport implementation, once persona-vvs2.1 makes one possible.

Endpoint: a named pipe under \\.\pipe\. The epic notes the previously specified name was corrected during the 2026-09-15 de-specification -- take the corrected form from the epic notes rather than from memory, and follow the SPIFFE npipe: endpoint address convention so a stock SPIFFE client can find it the way it would on any other Windows host.

Windows named pipe semantics differ from Unix sockets in ways that matter here and should be decided rather than discovered:
  - there is no filesystem path to unlink, so the stale-socket cleanup in
    hire-grpc/src/server.rs has no analogue. See persona-vvs2.5.
  - a pipe server pre-creates instances and each client connection consumes
    one; the accept loop shape is genuinely different from UnixListener.
  - the pipe's DACL is the access control. On Unix the socket's directory
    permissions restrict who may connect; the Windows equivalent is an
    explicit security descriptor, and getting it wrong is how a local
    workload API becomes reachable by any user on the machine.

That last point deserves the most care in this bead.
